transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been having these times, usually at night after work or if dinner’s been tense, where I start eating and it feels like I just can’t stop myself. It’s like the part of me that makes decisions shuts off—I can see myself reaching for more food, but I can’t make myself stop.
After one of these episodes where you feel unable to stop eating, do you ever try to 'undo' it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot to compensate?

Yeah. Sometimes after everyone’s gone to bed, I’ll make myself throw up in the bathroom, or I’ll take laxatives. I tell myself it’s just to undo the damage, but afterward I feel pretty embarrassed... and shaky.
On average, how many times per week have these binge-eating and purging episodes been happening, and how long has this pattern been going on?

For the last few months, it’s been most weeks—usually one night where I can’t stop eating, and then I try to make up for it afterward. Sometimes I throw up, sometimes laxatives, or I’ll skip meals or force myself to take a long walk.

latest_inference.note: Patient describes recurrent binge-eating episodes with regular compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxative use, fasting, excessive exercise) occurring most weeks for several months, consistent with Bulimia Nervosa. This pattern of compensatory behavior after bingeing rules out F50.9 (unspecified) and does not fit binge-eating disorder without purging.
